title: Every indecomposable Type I Berger subalgebra of split g2 in its standard seven-dimensional signature-(4,3) representation occurs as the exact holonomy algebra of a local metric
author: Anna Fino; Ines Kath
work: Local Type I Metrics with Holonomy in G2*
source_version: Official SIGMA 14 (2018) article 081, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2018.081; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: Berger admissibility does not by itself construct a metric with exactly the required reducible but indecomposable holonomy. The author derives adapted coframes, solves the torsion-free structure equations and then separates holonomy containment from equality using curvature and covariant curvature. The construction covers an entire parameterized classification, including non-full nilradicals and special solvable cases, rather than applying a general existence theorem.

source_check.note: The complete original main Theorem 1.1 and the entire author local Type-I metric realization construction are retained. The exact prior Berger representation list, adapted coframes, all torsion-free connection/PDE derivations, explicit metrics, curvature and covariant-curvature generators, and every final parameter/function table are included. The three previously realized cases are explicitly cited established background; the source final direct table checks are retained as stated without an independent rerun or generated reproof. All classified cases form one substantial main realization outcome, not separately counted parameter instances. The result is local exact signature-(4,3) holonomy, with no completeness/global/Type-II/III assertion. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: The entire paper was read, including the exact TypeI representation list2.2, all adapted-coframe/connection/PDE derivations3.2-3.22, every explicit metric example and the complete final parameter tables3.10. The maximal parabolic and all cases not containing the full nilradical have explicit curvature or covariant-curvature generators displayed, establishing exact holonomy by Ambrose-Singer. For the remaining full-nilradical cases, Section3.10 supplies every metric function and states that curvature generates in the listed easy cases, or curvature plus its first derivative in the four listed exceptions; these checks use the same explicit connection method as the worked examples and are left as bounded computations. The three already realized cases m,R*N semidirect m,s_(1/2) semidirect m are prior established results explicitly cited to[7]. No new classification proof of the prior list is claimed, and no individual case is counted separately.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.1 for indecomposable TypeI Berger subalgebras h of the split real g2* inside so(4,3), with TypeI meaning the socle of the standard seven-dimensional representation has dimension1. Exactly the prior classification list2.2 is realized by local signature-(4,3) metrics. The packet retains all new coordinate constructions and every final explicit function table, with the three prior realized cases cited as established background. It asserts local exact holonomy, not completeness, compactness, a global manifold or TypeII/III realization; no individual parameter case is a separate item.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: Section3.10 explicitly leaves the final curvature-generation checks for its fully specified metric functions as computations analogous to the worked examples. It distinguishes the cases generated by curvature alone from sl2,b-hat2,diag(1,0),s_lambda requiring its covariant derivative; no independently generated curvature calculations are inserted. The proof of Proposition3.10 has a literal sentence saying nabla b1=nabla b2=nabla b3=0 before referring to generally nonzero connection components from3.2; the displayed connection relations and coordinate construction are retained unchanged, and that sentence is not used as an extra vanishing conclusion.
